notes: On Windows the radio's window can no longer be resized by hand. The Desktop shortcut and the Startup entry now go through a small opener that starts the browser and then takes the window's resize grip and maximise box away -- no dragging the edges, no double-clicking the title bar, no Win+Arrow snapping -- while the radio stays free to size the window itself, which it must, because the themes are not the same height. It runs for under a second with its console minimised and exits; nothing is installed and nothing is left running, and a folder without it falls back to a shortcut aimed straight at the browser. There is no way to do this from the page: no web API makes a window non-resizable and no browser switch does either. On macOS and Linux the window can still be resized, and a size set by hand is no longer remembered -- the radio opens where you left it, at the size the theme wants. The window is also put back before the page is drawn rather than after the whole app has loaded, so it no longer appears at one place and jumps to another. The status line says just what the stream is doing; the frequency it used to repeat is already in its own readout two lines above. And the blinking dot in the update pill and the mark on the Settings control are one alert orange on every theme, rather than each cabinet's own colour.
